explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/656: for A ⊆ ℕ of positive upper density, must there be an infinite B ⊆ A and an integer t with {b₁ + b₂ : b₁ ≠ b₂ ∈ B} + t ⊆ A? Proved by Kra–Moreira–Richter–Robertson. The Lean statement: ∀ A with 0 < upperDensity, ∃ infinite B ⊆ A and t : ℤ such that for distinct b₁, b₂ ∈ B, b₁ + b₂ + t (computed in ℤ) equals some a ∈ A. This is exactly the requested inclusion with t allowed to be any integer, stated positively per the question convention. Faithful.
